newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Two Filipinos seeking wartime gold buried alive.
newsitem.headline: Two Filipinos seeking wartime gold buried alive.

text.p: Two Filipinos were buried alive while searching for wartime Japanese treasure that has already claimed dozens of lives, police said on Wednesday.
One other treasure hunter was injured when an eight-metre (25-foot) deep tunnel they were digging caved in on Tuesday in the southern Philippine city of General Santos.
Six companions managed to struggle to safety just before the tunnel collapsed.
Police quoted survivors as saying the two men who were killed had reported finding a chest they suspected contained the treasure and were trying to break it open when the tunnel collapsed.
Thousands of Filipinos have been digging for decades in various places across the Philippines in search of the so-called Yamashita treasure, the existence of which has never been proven.

The treasure hunt was triggered by rumours that Japanese General Tomoyuki Yamashita, hanged in 1946 as a war criminal, had looted the national treasuries of southeast Asian countries Japan conquered during World War Two and buried the booty in the Philippines.

The trove supposedly consists of bullion and jewellery worth between $100 and $200 billion. Many historians are sceptical about the treasure's existence and believe that whatever Yamashita siezed would have been sent back to Japan long before the war ended.
Dozens of Filipino hunters have died in cave-ins without finding any trace of it.
